creator: Chris Huber Reitz
name: English Wikipedia — Writing articles with large language models (content guideline)
quote: The use of large language models (LLMs) to generate or rewrite article content is strictly prohibited except for the uses as outlined below.
quote_label: Wikipedia:Writing articles with large language models (content guideline; RfC March 2026)

provenance.note: Exceptions: copyedits 'after human review' limited to 'spelling, punctuation, capitalisation, grammar, and other simple mistakes' and text must remain 'supported by the sources cited'; translation under WP:LLM-assisted translation. Stated rationale is itself verification economics: LLM text 'can be produced at a rate that makes review by other editors infeasible' -> partially (per-claim proof is cheap, but review capacity is the scarce resource). No disclosure requirement in this guideline (D3=0). Enforcement: 'Persistent use of large language models outside of the above exceptions is considered disruptive and will result in an editor being blocked from editing.' | Re-verified live 2026-09-27: Snapshot word-diff 09-20 vs 09-27: new revision (oldid 1375904828 -> 1376781070, last edited 26 Sept 2026) adds only a Latina interlanguage link (10 -> 11 languages). Guideline body text identical; coded quote present verbatim. | Re-verified live 2026-10-11: oldid 1378473005 (last edited 4 Oct 2026). Operative sentence now reads 'strictly prohibited' (was 'prohibited' through 09-27); 10-04 -> 10-11 diff is a hyphenation fix ('LLM generated' -> 'LLM-generated') and a moved 'Deletions' heading. Rationale quote corrected to live wording ('at a rate', not 'at such a rate').
